outline.description: This chapter lays out the factual background of Jimenez v. Bondi, tracks the procedural journey from initial entry through removal proceedings to the appeal before the Tenth Circuit, and identifies the precise issues presented on review.
subtopics: Petitioners’ identity, nationality, and immigration status
Political activities in Colombia and associated threats
Property dispute involving Don Rafa’s narco‑trafficking group
Timeline from arrival in the United States to issuance of Notices to Appear
Immigration Judge decision: denial of asylum/withholding/CAT
BIA affirmance and grounds for denial
Scope of the petition for review under § 1252(a)(1)
Key questions on appeal: past persecution, nexus, well‑founded fear

outline.chapter_title: Statutory Framework for Asylum and Withholding Removal
outline.description: This section explains how U.S. immigration law defines a refugee, sets the burden on applicants, delineates the three essential elements—past persecution, protected‑ground nexus, and government protection—and outlines how these elements are applied in both asylum and withholding removal contexts.
subtopics: "Refugee" definition under INA § 1101(a)(42)(A)
"Discretionary grant" nature of asylum under § 1158(b)(1)
"Well‑founded fear" as a prerequisite for withholding removal
"Burden of proof by preponderance" for asylum applicants
"Three‑prong test": past persecution incidents, protected ground linkage, state inability/unwillingness
"Rebuttable presumption" from proven past persecution
"Safe‑relocation exception" under § 1208.13(b)(1)(i)
"Standard of review": substantial‑evidence under § 1252(b)(4)(A)

outline.description: This chapter scrutinizes what constitutes past persecution under U.S. precedent, assesses whether Jimenez’s claims meet that threshold—including threats versus physical harm—and explains why the court found the record insufficient.
subtopics: "Persecution" definition in case law (Wiransane v. Ashcroft; Ritonga v. Holder)
"Threshold": more than mere threats or restrictions
"Cumulative effect” doctrine – multiple incidents considered together
"Threats alone” inadmissible per Karki v. Holder
"Physical harm” not mandatory but “offensive” suffering required
"Petitioners’ evidence”: phone calls, brochures, gun‑point incidents
"Emotional/psychological harm” – limited weight without accompanying physical injury
"Court’s conclusion”: substantial evidence supports BIA finding that no past persecution exists

outline.chapter_title: Assessing Nexus and Government Protection Claims
subtopics: "Nexus requirement": protected ground must be at least one central reason per Rivera‑Barrientos v. Holder (citation modified)
"Political opinion” test – centrality vs incidental role (Dallakoti v. Holder)
"Mixed‑motive cases” – primary vs secondary motives (OCV v. Bondi)
"Petitioners’ alleged nexus”: political affiliation versus personal conflict with Don Rafa
"Evidence against nexus”: lack of documentation that Don Rafa targeted them because of politics
"Government protection” analysis – notice requirement (§ 1101(a)(42)(B))
"Unwilling/unable test” – systemic failures versus isolated officer unhelpfulness (Aviles‑Gonzalez v. Garland; Osorio‑Moraes v. Garland)
"Petitioners’ reporting behavior” – minimal engagement with authorities explained in record
"Court’s ruling”: insufficient proof that Colombian authorities were unwilling or unable to protect them

outline.chapter_title: Safe Relocation Argument and Final Holding
subtopics: "Safe‑relocation standard”: preponderance test for relocating within home country (§ 1208.13(b)(1)(i))
"Fundamental change” versus internal relocation as rebuttal mechanisms (Rivera‑Barrientos)
"Petitioners’ potential relocation options”: family ties in Bogotá countryside demonstrate feasibility
"Court’s assessment”: safe relocation viable even if well‑founded fear existed
"Conclusion": denial of both asylum and withholding removal due to lack of all three elements;
'Denial' under § 1252(a)(1): appellate court affirms BIA findings based on substantial evidence;
'Significance' for future cases: clarifies thresholds for past persecution / nexus / government protection in Tenth Circuit;
